lobbyists.name: Adam William Chapdelaine
lobbyists.purpose: All legislative, administrative and regulatory matters pertaining to local government before the legislature and executive branch, including the following: • The general appropriations act and supplemental appropriations acts (House 1, the Governor's proposed fiscal 2026 state budget, and supplemental budgets for fiscal year 2025), and all legislation and regulations affecting local government finance, operations and administration; • State and local tax and revenue matters, including the property tax, state taxes and local-option taxing authority, payments-in-lieu-of taxes, municipal fees and charges and state fees and charges that would benefit local government, the administration of the state Lottery and distribution of Lottery proceeds, and the distribution of surtax revenue funding; • Municipal and education aid programs and funding, including Unrestricted General Government Aid, Chapter 70, charter school financing, special education funding, and school transportation reimbursements; • Funding and administration of capital programs benefiting local government including Chapter 90, water-related funding and bond authorizations, the school building assistance program, and municipal infrastructure needs; • Education matters affecting the operation and financing of municipal, regional and other school districts, including vocational and charter schools; • Personnel and labor matters affecting cities and towns, including Civil Service, other post employment benefits (OPEB), municipal health insurance, unemployment insurance (UI), collective bargaining, training, certification and management of public employees, workplace safety, and the composition of the commonwealth employment relations board; • Human services and public health, including delivery of public health services and matters related to public emergencies; • Energy matters, including solar and other renewable energy matters; • Environmental matters, including the cost-benefit analyses of environmental rules and regulations, environmental permitting and permit approval procedures, sustainable water resource funds, recycling and solid water management, PFAS mitigation and other water and land contamination matters; • Municipal planning, permitting, zoning, housing and other matters related to local and regional land use regulation and economic development; • Public works, including use of public rights-of-way and the municipal purchase of utility poles; • All matters related to the administration of local government, including but not limited to elections and actions by local legislative bodies, municipal control over liquor licenses, municipal authority regarding the cannabis industry, the administration of veteran’s benefits, and the modernization of municipal government operations; In these efforts, this legislative agent will communicate with every member of the Massachusetts House of Representatives and Senate, and all corresponding executive branch officials.

lobbyists.purpose: Eneida Román, CEO of We Are ALX, will serve as the organization’s designated lobbyist to advocate for policies and budgetary measures that advance Latino prosperity, racial equity, and economic mobility in Massachusetts. Her lobbying activities will focus on increasing equitable access to state-funded economic development programs, small business support, workforce development initiatives, and culturally responsive education and childcare services for Latino communities. Areas of legislative and budgetary interest include, but are not limited to: Economic and workforce development legislation that expands access to capital, grants, and training for Minority- and Women-Owned Business Enterprises (MWBEs), particularly Latino-owned businesses. Education and early childhood policies that support Latino educators, family childcare providers, and dual-language learners. Support for public funding, including line items in the Massachusetts state budget, that align with ALX’s mission to elevate Latino leadership and prosperity. Engagement with Executive Office of Economic Development, Executive Office of Education, and the Governor’s Latino Empowerment Council, among others. ALX’s advocacy includes direct engagement with legislators, committee chairs, and agency officials, including members of the Massachusetts Black and Latino Legislative Caucus. Specific legislation and bill numbers will be added as filed and relevant to our organizational priorities.
